pr_title: opt: push limit into FK and self-joins in more cases
pr_body:
#### opt: more accurate join multiplicity with FKs and self-joins

When calculating join multiplicity in the presence of a foreign key, it
was previously possible for the incorrect base table to be selected from
the right expression, in the case that the right expression contained a
self-join. The base table selected was incorrect because it did not
contain the equality column from the join filter. This prevented the
optimizer from determining that these joins preserve all rows from the
left side of the join, which could prevent further optimization of a
query.

Now, only the right equality columns are passed to `checkForeignKeyCase`
which ensures that the correct base table is selected. This is safe
because `verifyFiltersAreValidEqualities` has already checked that the
right equality columns are unfiltered in the right expression, so the
same checks in `checkForeignKeyCase` are redundant.

Release note (performance improvement): The optimizer better optimizes
queries that include both foreign key joins and self-joins.

#### opt: push limit into FK and self-joins in more cases

Previously, a constant equality condition pushed into both sides of a
foreign key join or self-join would prevent a limit from being pushed
into the left side of the join. This was because the multiplicity
builder could not determine that right filter would not remove any
values also removed by the left filter. Without the join being labelled
as left-preserving, the limit could not be pushed down.

The multiplicity builder has been updated to recognize a few additional
cases where left rows are preserved in foreign key joins and self-joins,
allowing a limit to be pushed into the left side of the join. Currently,
the multiplicity builder only recognizes cases where corresponding left
and right columns are held equal to the same constant value. It is
possible to extend this to more complex inequalities and boolean
expressions, but this is left as a TODO for now.

Fixes #74419

Release note (performance improvement): A LIMIT can now be pushed below
a foreign key join or self-join in more cases, which may result in more
efficient query plans.

Previously, mgartner (Marcus Gartner) wrote…
Updated. With the change to your suggestion that **the left filters must imply the right filters**, not the inverse. For example: ``` FK JOIN ON x = y left filters: x > 0 right filters: y > 10 (imply the left filters) Not valid: x in [0,10] will not match rows on the right FK JOIN ON x = y left filters: x > 10 (imply the right filters) right filters: y > 0 Valid: all values of x will have a matching y on the right ``` > I try to think whether there are any possible problems with composite columns. I added a warning to the TODO about composite columns.
Minor typo in that first example. It should read "Not valid: x in **(0, 10]** will not match rows on the right."

Thanks for all the great feedback - the complicated logic demands clear comments.

bors r+

issue_context.title: sql: presence of foreign key breaks limit pushdown through join
issue_context.body:
In our TPC-E implementation, we began validating foreign keys. This led to a regression of one of the query plans. For the following query:
```sql
SELECT
  t_id,
  ...
  ct_name
FROM
  trade
  LEFT HASH JOIN trade_type ON tt_id = t_tt_id
  LEFT LOOKUP JOIN security ON s_symb = t_s_symb
  LEFT LOOKUP JOIN settlement ON se_t_id = t_id
  LEFT LOOKUP JOIN cash_transaction ON ct_t_id = t_id
WHERE
  t_s_symb = 'ALAN'AND t_dts >= '2005-12-20 13:57:46.951'AND t_dts <= '2006-02-27 09:15:00'
ORDER BY
  t_dts ASC
LIMIT
  20;
```
The plan used to look like:
```
  • render
  │ estimated row count: 20
  │
  └── • lookup join (left outer)
      │ estimated row count: 20
      │ table: cash_transaction@cash_transaction_pkey
      │ equality: (t_id) = (ct_t_id)
      │ equality cols are key
      │
      └── • lookup join (left outer)
          │ estimated row count: 20
          │ table: settlement@settlement_pkey
          │ equality: (t_id) = (se_t_id)
          │ equality cols are key
          │
          └── • lookup join (left outer)
              │ estimated row count: 20
              │ table: security@security_pkey_replicated_0
              │ equality: (t_s_symb) = (s_symb)
              │ equality cols are key
              │ pred: s_symb = 'ALAN'
              │
              └── • sort
                  │ estimated row count: 20
                  │ order: +t_dts
                  │
                  └── • hash join
                      │ estimated row count: 20
                      │ equality: (t_tt_id) = (tt_id)
                      │ right cols are key
                      │
                      ├── • scan
                      │     estimated row count: 20 (<0.01% of the table; stats collected 2 hours ago)
                      │     table: trade@trade_t_s_symb_t_dts_idx
                      │     spans: [/'ALAN'/'2005-12-20 13:57:46.951' - /'ALAN'/'2006-02-27 09:15:00']
                      │     limit: 20
                      │
                      └── • scan
                            estimated row count: 5 (100% of the table; stats collected 2 hours ago)
                            table: trade_type@trade_type_pkey_replicated_0
                            spans: FULL SCAN
```
Once we validated the foreign key from `trade` to `security`, the plan switched to:
```
  • render
  │ estimated row count: 20
  │
  └── • lookup join (left outer)
      │ estimated row count: 20
      │ table: cash_transaction@cash_transaction_pkey
      │ equality: (t_id) = (ct_t_id)
      │ equality cols are key
      │
      └── • lookup join (left outer)
          │ estimated row count: 20
          │ table: settlement@settlement_pkey
          │ equality: (t_id) = (se_t_id)
          │ equality cols are key
          │
          └── • limit
              │ estimated row count: 20
              │ count: 20
              │
              └── • lookup join
                  │ estimated row count: 23,092
                  │ table: security@security_pkey_replicated_0
                  │ equality: (t_s_symb) = (s_symb)
                  │ equality cols are key
                  │ pred: s_symb = 'ALAN'
                  │
                  └── • sort
                      │ estimated row count: 23,092
                      │ order: +t_dts
                      │
                      └── • hash join
                          │ estimated row count: 23,092
                          │ equality: (t_tt_id) = (tt_id)
                          │ right cols are key
                          │
                          ├── • scan
                          │     estimated row count: 23,092 (0.03% of the table; stats collected 1 hour ago)
                          │     table: trade@trade_t_s_symb_t_dts_idx
                          │     spans: [/'ALAN'/'2005-12-20 13:57:46.951' - /'ALAN'/'2006-02-27 09:15:00']
                          │
                          └── • scan
                                estimated row count: 5 (100% of the table; stats collected 1 hour ago)
                                table: trade_type@trade_type_pkey_replicated_0
                                spans: FULL SCAN
```
Notice that the limit is no longer pushed into the scan on the `trade` table, so instead of scanning 20 rows, we now scan ~23k and join these with their corresponding `security` row before applying the limit.

This appears to be somehow related to the join predicate that we finger on the `security` table lookup join.

Statement bundle: [stmt-bundle-724966946692005890.zip](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/files/7809795/stmt-bundle-724966946692005890.zip).
comments:
I think the problem is that the validated foreign key lets us simplify the security lookup join into an inner join. At that point, we no longer know that it's ok to push the limit down because of the issue mentioned here: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/21171#issuecomment-558593531
As you suspected @nvanbenschoten it's the `s_symb = 'ALAN'` condition that's the problem. This filter on the right input doesn't prevent left rows from finding matches because of the corresponding `t_s_symb = 'ALAN'` filter on the left input, but we don't currently have a way to prove this.

Thanks for looking into this @DrewKimball!

@nvanbenschoten as a workaround for now, you can use the `IGNORE_FOREIGN_KEYS` hint to prevent the optimizer from making optimizations based on the knowledge of foreign keys. Foreign key checks will still occur so you can be sure that they won't be violated. Here's the query with the hint:

```sql
SELECT
  t_id,
  t_ca_id,
  t_exec_name,
  t_is_cash,
  t_trade_price::FLOAT8,
  t_qty,
  t_dts,
  t_tt_id,
  tt_name,
  s_name,
  se_amt::FLOAT8,
  se_cash_due_date,
  se_cash_type,
  ct_amt::FLOAT8,
  ct_dts,
  ct_name
FROM
  trade@{IGNORE_FOREIGN_KEYS}
  LEFT HASH JOIN trade_type ON tt_id = t_tt_id
  LEFT LOOKUP JOIN security ON s_symb = t_s_symb
  LEFT LOOKUP JOIN settlement ON se_t_id = t_id
  LEFT LOOKUP JOIN cash_transaction ON ct_t_id = t_id
WHERE
  t_s_symb = 'ALAN' AND t_dts >= '2005-12-20 13:57:46.951' AND t_dts <= '2006-02-27 09:15:00'
ORDER BY t_dts ASC
LIMIT 20
```

review_comments: I think I'm missing a check that the leftCol and rightCol are unfiltered in the inputs of the Select expressions.
